# A model that outlives its timeout is stopped with its whole process tree
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #114, sha256:bc2b9e1df3f71a88be30f23447653745b01b0391e7264807badd7240e43490c3). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-27 (commit a7bec47, authored by Codex; a model that outlives its timeout is stopped with its whole process tree in both arms and the real hung Grok prompt now ends at the limit; Decider D83 passed)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; benchmark robustness in both arms)
- **Milestone:** Measure first: does Phrase beat plain C# on tokens and attempts at an equal or better pass rate?
- **Source:** Found 2026-10-27 in the smoke of the holdout run (card 102): Grok on the first holdout prompt stayed alive for 29 minutes in the Phrase arm and over 7 minutes in the plain C# arm with --timeout-ms 300000, using about 4 CPU seconds in total (idle, not computing); run directly with the same prompt file the Grok CLI also did not exit in 180 seconds, while a trivial prompt returns in 3 seconds. A model that outlives its timeout must be stopped with its whole process tree in both arms, or one hung driver stalls a long run.
- **Depends on:** 113
- **Story:** As Riley, I want a model that does not finish within its timeout stopped with every process it started, so that one hung driver cannot stall a scored run for an hour.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a fake model command run through the same shell path the real CLIs use (a command-line wrapper that starts a grandchild process which ignores stdin, holds the output pipes open and sleeps), and a prompt of about 10 KB, When the run uses a 3-second timeout, Then each arm records the attempt as a timeout, the run ends within 20 seconds, and the grandchild is gone afterwards (the fake records its own process id and the test checks that exact id)
  2. Given a timeout, When it fires, Then the row or the attempt feedback says the model timed out with the limit and the elapsed time, the attempt counts toward the attempt cap, and the tokens consumed so far are charged as for any failed attempt
  3. Given models that finish within their timeout, When this card is merged, Then their rows, prompt hashes and launch arguments are unchanged in both arms

## Context

- Only exact process ids recorded by the test or the harness are stopped, never a process found by name. Windows: the model is started through cmd.exe /c; a tree kill that stops only the shell leaves node and the CLI alive holding the pipes, which is the suspected failure; also stop waiting for the output pipes after the kill so a surviving grandchild cannot block the run.
- Tests use fake commands only (no real model). Applies to tools/Phrase.Bench and tools/Phrase.BenchCs. Every nested dotnet process inherits MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1.
